plugins.name: zsh-wordsplit-guard
plugins.description: Catches commands that run differently from bash when the Bash tool uses zsh. A loop over a bare expansion (`for x in $var`) runs once over the whole string, since zsh does not word-split it; a glob or a path around the expansion (`for f in $D/*.log`) is left alone. Likewise a loop variable over quoted multi-word items (`for c in "a.py -v" "b.py"`) used unquoted in the body (`python3 $c`) stays one word. So does a command stored in a variable (`DC="docker compose -f a.yml"`) and run as `$DC build`, which zsh looks up as one command name. An unquoted argument (`cmd $files`) is also caught when the same call previously assigns the variable a multi-word quoted value or command substitution; quote it for one argument, or split explicitly. Also caught: `$name:` followed by a history modifier, even inside double quotes; brace the name as `${name}:…`. Also caught: an unquoted word or assignment value starting with `=` (`echo =====`, `[ a == b ]`, `v==x`), which zsh expands to a command path, and a glob in a `--flag=value` word (`--include=*.md`), which aborts on `no matches found` — both rewritten in place when the word is literal text, denied otherwise; and denied: parentheses in a `${var/pattern/…}` pattern, which zsh reads as a glob group; bash's `${!name}` forms, which zsh aborts on or reads as `$!`; and bash's `${v@Q}` transformations, which zsh aborts on. Each deny message names the form to use instead. The loop and stored-value rules opt out per call with `[nosplit]` in the description, or session-wide with ALLOW_ZSH_NOSPLIT=1; the other rules opt out by the rewrite they apply or name.
